measured_for: Taiwan, national: the couple as one insured person plus one dependent in Category 6 (regional population, not employed), after the 6-month wait for a foreign resident with a residence permit
note: kind=statutory; 826 (insured, 60% of the NT$1,377 average premium) + 826 (one dependent) = NT$1,652 a month. Fixed, no income test. Extra: 2.11% supplementary premium on dividends, interest and rent paid by Taiwanese payers when a single payment reaches NT$20,000 (cap NT$10m per payment); capital gains on shares are not in the base; whether foreign-source dividends are withheld was not found. Foreign residents join only after 6 months of continuous residence with a residence permit; until then private cover is needed. The average premium has been NT$1,377 since 2021-01-01.

measured_for: South Korea, national: one household (the couple) enrolled as regional subscribers after 6 months' residence, with no Korean income or property
note: kind=statutory; floor, not a fixed fee: NHIS calculates the household premium like a Korean one (7.19% x monthly income + property points x KRW 211.5, plus long-term care at 0.9448/7.19 of the health premium) and, if that is lower than the foreign-regional average, charges the average: KRW 140,210 health + KRW 18,420 long-term care = KRW 158,630 a month per household. Income and property raise it above the floor; a household head with F-5 (permanent resident) or F-6 (marriage migrant) status has no floor and pays by the formula only. Foreigners join after 6 months' residence. Whether foreign-source investment income is counted was not confirmed.

measured_for: Costa Rica, national: couple enrolled in the CCSS as voluntary insured (resident, no local employer), health part (SEM) only, on a declared income of CRC 1,125,000 a month (the US$2,500 rentista minimum at CRC 450 per US$)
note: kind=statutory; rule = rate of the declared-income band x whole declared income, health (SEM) member share. Band 3 (CRC 746,186 to 1,492,369) health 6.24%: 6.24% x 1,125,000 = CRC 70,200 a month. The pension (IVM) share in the same band is 7.53% = CRC 84,713, so SEM+IVM = 13.77% = CRC 154,913 (the combined figure residency guides quote). Health shares by band: 2.89% / 4.33% / 6.24% / 8.02% / 10.69% at income ceilings CRC 346,789 / 746,185 / 1,492,369 / 2,238,554 / above; at CRC 2,238,555 and above the health share is 10.69% = CRC 239,000 or more. Depends on the income declared to Migración. The spouse is normally covered as a family member of the principal (secondary source, not checked in CCSS text). Public CCSS care only; many residents add private cover.

measured_for: Tokyo's 23 special wards (Koto ward FY2026 rates, shared by 20 wards): two NHI members aged 40 to 64, fixed per-person part only
note: kind=statutory; per person per year: medical 47,600 + elderly-support 17,600 + care (ages 40 to 64) 17,800 + child-support 1,873 = JPY 84,873; two people = 169,746 a year = JPY 14,145.5 a month. Added on top, per person, from the previous year's income after a JPY 430,000 deduction: 7.51% medical + 2.80% support + 2.43% care + 0.27% child support = 13.01%, with annual caps of 670,000 + 260,000 + 170,000 + 30,000 per person. A new arrival with no Japanese income record is billed the flat part first (Koto newsletter, June 2026). Investment income in a Japanese withholding account that is not declared is left out of the base; if declared it counts. Low-income reductions on the flat part (70%, 50%, 20%) apply only below income limits. Rates differ by municipality.

measured_for: Canada, national: a couple who are new permanent residents, provincial public health insurance; no premium for the insurance itself in the provinces read (Ontario, British Columbia, Québec)
note: kind=statutory; permanent residents qualify. Waiting periods: Ontario none ('There is no longer a waiting period for OHIP'); British Columbia the rest of the arrival month plus two months; Québec up to 3 months, and private cover is advised for that gap. Premiums: BC eliminated MSP premiums on 2020-01-01; Ontario has no OHIP premium but an income-tax Health Premium of C$0 (taxable income up to C$20,000) to C$900 (over C$200,600) per person, i.e. up to C$150 a month for the couple; Québec has a compulsory prescription-drug plan premium of C$0 to C$789 per person a year (2026-27) through the tax return unless covered by a private drug plan. Other provinces not read. Most residents add private cover for drugs, dental, vision and private rooms; no published rate table was found.
quote: There is no longer a waiting period for OHIP coverage. If you are eligible, you will have immediate health insurance coverage. … are a permanent resident (formerly called a “landed immigrant”)

measured_for: New Zealand, national: a couple holding resident visas, publicly funded health and disability services
note: kind=statutory; holders of a residence class visa, resident visa or permanent resident visa are eligible for publicly funded services with no waiting period and no premium (hospital care, subsidised GP visits; part-charges for GP visits, prescriptions and dental apply and were not priced). ACC (levy-funded, in the tax system) covers accidents. New regulations from 2026-12-01 leave residents unchanged. Private insurance (Southern Cross, nib, Accuro, AIA, Partners Life) publishes no price list; a broker's October 2026 sample quote for Southern Cross Wellbeing One with a NZ$500 excess is NZ$57.84 a fortnight at 40 and NZ$101.01 at 50 for a woman (age 45 not shown), labelled broker cross-check.
quote: New Zealand resident class visa holders. You are eligible for if you have either: a residence class visa, a resident visa, a permanent resident visa.

measured_for: Chile, national: couple affiliated to FONASA, the public insurer (the non-earning spouse as a dependant), at the maximum legal contribution: 7% of taxable income capped at UF 90, i.e. UF 6.3 a month at UF = CLP 41,350.42 (2026-11-17)
note: kind=statutory; rule: legal health contribution = 7% of the member's taxable income (remuneration, pension or declared voluntary base), capped at UF 90 a month, so at most UF 6.3 = CLP 260,508 a month for the household (6.3 x 41,350.42). The couple pays less if the declared base is lower (7% of base; the Superintendencia also states contributions cannot be below 7% of the minimum wage, from a search summary not saved) but FONASA's copayment tier follows income. A spouse without income is normally a dependant (carga) at no extra premium (not verified in an official page). Residents can join FONASA with a residence application in progress. Many higher-income residents choose an ISAPRE (private) plan instead: its price is a plan base price in UF times an age and sex factor, set by each plan; no ISAPRE price table was captured.
quote: La cotización legal para salud corresponde al 7% de la remuneración o renta imponible de la persona afiliada. La remuneración o renta imponible tiene un tope mensual de UF 90 …, por lo que la cotización legal máxima para salud es de UF 6,3 al mes.

measured_for: Peru, national: two residents aged 30 to 59 each insured under EsSalud's voluntary +Salud Seguro Potestativo, S/138 each (the spouse's rate is assumed equal; the sources say dependants cost extra without a figure)
note: kind=statutory; voluntary public insurance open to any resident, Peruvian or foreign, not insured through an employer. Age band 30-59: S/138 a month per titular (0-17 S/137, 18-29 S/132, 60+ S/215); 2 x 138 = S/276 a month. 3-month waiting period for non-urgent care (secondary sources; a source says up to 12 months for scheduled surgery and pre-existing conditions). Spouse as 'derechohabiente' needs form F-1010 and carries an extra charge that the saved table does not give; treat 276 as an estimate. EsSalud hospitals are crowded; wealthy residents mostly buy private plans (Rimac, Pacífico) whose rates were not found in a published table.

measured_for: Colombia, national: contributory-regime health insurance (EPS) for an independent person or capital renter who is a resident, at the minimum base (1 SMMLV); a spouse without income is a beneficiary
note: kind=statutory; floor row. Rule: health contribution = 12.5% x IBC; IBC for independent workers and rentistas de capital = 40% of monthly income received (net of real or presumed costs), never below 1 SMMLV (COP 1,750,905 in 2026) nor above 25 SMMLV. Floor: 12.5% x 1,750,905 = COP 218,863 a month. Worked example, income COP 20,000,000 a month with 27.5% presumed costs: IBC = 20,000,000 x (1 - 0.275) x 0.40 = 5,800,000; health = 12.5% x 5,800,000 = COP 725,000. Cap: 12.5% x 25 x 1,750,905 = COP 5,471,578. The income-dependent part is the whole amount above the floor. Pension contributions (16%) are separate and not counted. The spouse is added as a beneficiary at no extra premium (standard rule, not checked in a saved source). Whether foreign-source capital income counts, and the presumed-cost percentage in force (27.5% or 28.08%), were not confirmed. Private prepaid plans (Colsanitas, Sura) are the usual choice for the wealthy; no published table found.
quote: Para los trabajadores independientes que desarrollen actividades por cuenta propia, celebren contratos distintos a los de prestación de servicios o sean rentistas de capital, el IBC será el 40 % del valor mensual de los ingresos causados o percibidos … [IBC minimum] $1.750.905 [health 12.5%]

measured_for: Australia, national: a couple who are new permanent residents, Medicare (public cover)
note: kind=statutory; permanent visa holders living in Australia are eligible for Medicare, and applicants for permanent residency can enrol from the date of application (Services Australia, via a search extract). No premium: Medicare is funded by the Medicare levy, 2% of taxable income (not read in a saved ATO page; belongs to the tax agent), plus a Medicare levy surcharge of 1% to 1.5% of income for high earners without private hospital cover (thresholds not captured). Holding a private hospital policy (see the private row) removes the surcharge. Overseas Visitors Health Cover applies only to temporary visa holders and no published table exists.
quote: Permanent residents are eligible once they have been granted permanent residency and are living in Australia [search extract of the Services Australia page]

measured_for: Dubai: two members on the Essential Benefits Plan, the regulator's minimum plan, at the top of the Index Rate band (AED 750 per member per year) before VAT
note: kind=statutory; compulsory: health cover is mandatory for residents in Dubai and a sponsor must buy at least the Essential Benefits Plan. Index Rate band AED 550 to 750 per member per year plus VAT, with insurers allowed to vary by AED 25 either way. Couple at the top of the band: 2 x 750 = AED 1,500 a year = AED 125 a month, plus 5% VAT (not in the amount); at the bottom AED 1,100 a year = AED 91.67 a month. The plan is a minimum (capped annual limit, local network); a couple like this would buy a comprehensive plan, for which no published age table was found (Daman, AXA Gulf, Sukoon and Orient quote online or through brokers).
quote: The Index Rate (IR) band is set at AED 550 – 750/- per member per year plus VAT (in addition, to any other charges). The variation of + or – AED 25/- around the submitted IR remains. [DHA circular, Table of Benefits for Essential Benefits Plan, effective 1 Jan 2025]

measured_for: Mexico, national: two people aged 40 to 49 on the IMSS voluntary family health insurance (Modalidad 33), annual fee paid in advance
note: kind=statutory; voluntary, not compulsory: IMSS Seguro de Salud para la Familia, age 40-49 MXN 13,800 a year per person (table published December 2025); couple 2 x 13,800 = MXN 27,600 a year = MXN 2,300 a month. Press reports of 2026 fees imply about +4%. Covers medical, surgical, pharmacy, hospital and maternity care; pre-existing conditions block entry and some conditions have waiting periods. Foreign residents with a residence permit can enrol (rule not read in a saved IMSS page). Most expats buy private 'gastos médicos mayores' instead: no insurer publishes an age table (AXA, GNP, Mapfre, Metlife quote through their websites or brokers; CONDUSEF offers a simulator).
